title: Add a "When inactive with no apps blocking sleep or screen locking" condition
line: The "When inactive" command in Power Management can now be set to not run while an app is blocking sleep or screen locking.
explanation: PowerDevil's Run Script action ran the "When inactive" command on every idle timeout without checking inhibitions, unlike dimming and screen turn-off, so a screensaver script started over a video that was blocking screen locking. There was no way to make it respect those blocks. The change adds an "Even when apps are blocking sleep or screen locking" checkbox under the command (checked by default, so existing setups behave as before); when unchecked, the idle timeout skips the command while any sleep or screen-locking inhibition is active.

commits.message:
runscript: allow skipping the inactivity command while apps block it

The "When inactive" command ran even while an app was blocking sleep or
screen locking, so a screensaver script could start over a video. Add a
checkbox to the command's settings that, when unchecked, skips it then.

BUG: 521388

media.caption: Master: the "When inactive" command has no option about apps blocking sleep or screen locking; it ran after 10 s idle even with a screen-locking block active.
With the fix: new "Even when apps are blocking sleep or screen locking" checkbox; unchecked, the command no longer runs while a block is active.

reviews.text: Well-structured, minimal PowerDevil change that solves the requested use case without duplicating the inactivity command/timeout controls. Checking both InterruptSession and ChangeScreenSettings in RunScript::onIdleTimeout matches the bug's sleep and screen-locking scope, defaulting InhibitIdleTimeoutCommandWhenAppsBlock to false preserves backwards compatibility, and the KCM checkbox mirrors the existing lid-action checkbox style, KCM.SettingStateBinding wiring, and accessibility pattern cleanly.
